extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from primary text, figure captions, methods, and supplement captions; automated pending-review placeholders removed.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: BacSp222 causes dose-dependent leakage of GFP from susceptible bacterial cells, supporting membrane disruption as a lytic antibacterial mechanism rather than a discrete-pore-only claim.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: BacSp222 against GFP-expressing Bacillus subtilis and Staphylococcus aureus; Escherichia coli included as resistant/low-susceptibility comparison
mechanism_claims.limitations: Detailed membrane biophysics is discussed as generalized disruption; exact pore architecture is not claimed.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: BacSp222 damages mammalian cell membrane integrity at cytotoxic concentrations, supported by LDH release and PI/FDA microscopy in source text and figures.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Human skin fibroblasts, keratinocytes, HeLa/ASC supplementary context, and murine macrophage-like cells
mechanism_claims.limitations: Exact LD50 insert values from figure images are not machine-normalized beyond text-supported approximate values.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: At nanomolar concentrations BacSp222 modulates murine macrophage-like cells by enhancing IFNγ-induced nitric oxide release; BacSp222 alone induced NO only in P388D1 at 100 and 1000 nM and did not enhance LPS-induced NO.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: P388D1 and RAW264.7 murine macrophage-like cells
mechanism_claims.limitations: The source supports functional NO modulation, not a complete upstream receptor/signaling pathway assignment.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: BacSp222 did not activate the tested FPRL1 receptor overexpressed in recombinant CHO-K1 cells, so FPRL1 activation is preserved as a negative/rejected mechanism for this paper.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Negative FPRL1 result does not exclude other host receptors or indirect IFNγ pathway priming.
